strengths.item: Introduces a clear and meaningful formulation for adaptive domain randomization: maximizing the entropy of the dynamics distribution subject to a minimum success-probability constraint.

Positions the method well against LSDR, AutoDR, and self-paced curriculum/domain-randomization approaches, with a plausible distinction from methods requiring reference distributions, target distributions, boundary evaluations, or real-world data.

The contribution is not only conceptual but also practical, combining the objective with KL trust-region updates, importance-sampled success estimates from already collected training data, backup optimization, history-conditioned policies, and asymmetric critics.

Empirical results suggest potential impact for sim-to-real reinforcement learning, including improved performance over relevant baselines on MuJoCo sim-to-sim tasks and a real Franka Panda pushing task.

weaknesses.item: The broad idea of gradually expanding a training distribution based on policy competence is related to prior adaptive domain randomization and curriculum-learning methods, so the novelty is more of a clean reformulation/generalization than a wholly new paradigm.
The impact is primarily within simulation-to-real reinforcement learning and dynamics randomization; the contribution may be narrower outside this setting.

Some implementation choices, such as history conditioning, asymmetric critics, trust regions, and backup updates, are useful but individually incremental or borrowed from existing RL/curriculum practices.
The novelty assessment relies mainly on the paper’s own related-work framing rather than independently verified retrieval over all prior work.

dimension_review.evidence_summary: The paper proposes DORAEMON, which learns a domain-randomization distribution by maximizing entropy while enforcing a minimum success probability. Compared with LSDR, AutoDR, and self-paced curriculum learning, the paper claims to avoid a fixed reference or target distribution, real-world data, and boundary-biased expansion heuristics. Experiments on six MuJoCo tasks and a PandaPush sim-to-real robotic manipulation task report better or faster convergence and stronger success rates than No-DR, Fixed-DR, LSDR, and AutoDR. The Q&A assessment found the exact entropy-maximization-with-success-constraint formulation meaningfully novel relative to the closest methods described, while noting conceptual overlap with curriculum-style distribution expansion.
dimension_review.rationale: The contribution is good: the paper provides a well-motivated and practically useful objective for adaptive domain randomization, along with a complete algorithm and convincing empirical demonstrations including sim-to-real transfer. Its strongest novelty lies in replacing reference/target-distribution or boundary-expansion approaches with entropy maximization under a success constraint. However, the work builds on existing ideas in adaptive domain randomization, performance-gated curricula, and robust RL, so it is better characterized as a significant reformulation and integration rather than an excellent, field-defining contribution. A score of 3 is appropriate.
